cases.note: §10, quoted: the Hub records not "robot X is online" but "robot X is running image sha256:…, policy sha256:…, against body sha256:…". This is that sentence, and it is frozen as bytes because it is the one an incident investigation reads.
cases.expected: {"complete":true,"sentence":"dev_7 is running image `sha256:aaaa`, policy `sha256:bbbb`, against body `sha256:cccc`.","unmeasured":[]}

cases.note: Running nothing is a complete and true report, not a missing field. A fleet console that showed this identically to a robot whose policy digest could not be read would be reporting unknown software as none.
cases.expected: {"complete":true,"sentence":"dev_7 is running image `sha256:aaaa`, no policy, against body `sha256:cccc`.","unmeasured":[]}

cases.note: The other half of the pair above. Same robot, same shape, and the two must not render the same — which is the entire reason `nothing` and `unmeasured` are separate states.
cases.expected: {"complete":false,"sentence":"dev_7 is running image `sha256:aaaa`, an unmeasured policy (the runtime is not answering), against body `sha256:cccc`.","unmeasured":["policy"]}

cases.note: §1: guest runs "a container beside the vendor stack". There is no Skynet OS image to measure and reporting one would be inventing a digest — so `nothing` is the true answer and the report is complete.
cases.expected: {"complete":true,"sentence":"dev_7 is running no OS image, policy `sha256:bbbb`, against body `sha256:cccc`.","unmeasured":[]}

cases.note: §27’s `kernel: down`. Reporting a body digest here would attest joint ratings nothing is applying, which is the failure the whole descriptor chain exists to prevent.
cases.expected: {"complete":true,"sentence":"dev_7 is running image `sha256:aaaa`, no policy, against no body.","unmeasured":[]}

cases.note: No device id, because nothing has issued one. The sentence names "This robot" rather than inventing an identifier — and it is still produced, because a robot bringing itself up needs to be able to say what it is running before anybody has paired it.
cases.expected: {"complete":true,"sentence":"This robot is running image `sha256:aaaa`, no policy, against body `sha256:cccc`.","unmeasured":[]}

cases.note: The branch a caller reaches by constructing the state without the sentence. Rendered as the absence it is rather than as an empty pair of brackets.
cases.expected: {"complete":false,"sentence":"dev_7 is running an unmeasured OS image, policy `sha256:bbbb`, against body `sha256:cccc`.","unmeasured":["os_image"]}

cases.note: §13’s rule, applied to a report rather than to a recording: the one most likely to have a hole in it is the one covering whatever made the hole. A check-in withheld for want of a digest is a robot the fleet believes is offline, which turns a named gap into a silence nobody can tell from a dead machine.

os_image.why: the slot could not be read

cases.expected: {"complete":false,"sentence":"dev_7 is running an unmeasured OS image (the slot could not be read), an unmeasured policy, against an unmeasured body (no descriptor is loaded).","unmeasured":["embodiment","os_image","policy"]}

cases.note: A caller bug, and the rendering is what stops it becoming a lie: an empty pair of backticks is read as a digest, and this reads as the absence it is. The report is still complete, because the caller said it measured — this file will not overrule a measurement it did not take.
cases.expected: {"complete":true,"sentence":"This robot is running an unnamed OS image, no policy, against no body.","unmeasured":[]}
